plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Robustel switch. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, temperature, and interface traffic (enterprise PEN 39699).
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports the one-second CPU utilization of the Robustel MG460 industrial switch (rosSysutilStatusCpuLoadAverage1sec) as a 0-100 percentage. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, forwarding instability, or attack traffic.

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage_10s
metrics.description: This metric reports the ten-second CPU utilization of the Robustel MG460 industrial switch (rosSysutilStatusCpuLoadAverage10sec) as a 0-100 percentage. It is a longer-window companion to the one-second headline CPU metric.

metrics.name: device_memory_total
metrics.description: This metric reports the total physical memory of the Robustel MG460 industrial switch in bytes (rosSysutilStatusMemoryTotalKb, converted from kilobytes).

metrics.name: device_memory_used
metrics.description: This metric reports the used physical memory of the Robustel MG460 industrial switch in bytes (rosSysutilStatusMemoryUsedKb, converted from kilobytes).

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: This metric reports overall memory utilization of the Robustel MG460 industrial switch, computed as used / total * 100. Vendor kilobyte units cancel in the ratio. High memory usage may indicate leaks, oversized MAC/ARP tables, or insufficient capacity.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports each ROS-SYSUTIL temperature monitor sensor of the Robustel MG460 industrial switch (rosSysutilStatusTemperatureMonitorTemperature) in degrees Celsius. Index board=0 / junction=1. Sustained high temperature can indicate cooling failure or an overheated environment.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
